headline: High-risk filesystem and code-execution overlap: Open Interpreter can alter the user machine while Taipy lacks documented isolation or write controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads and writes the user filesystem and uses clipboard/stdin, so malicious content can be fed into its instruction stream. Taipy has no documented input isolation or provenance controls in the profile, so if its outputs are copied into Open Interpreter, prompt injection is plausible. The pathway is interaction-based, not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF Taipy output is copied into Open Interpreter via clipboard or files
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent reduced confirmation
mitigations: Disable auto-run in Open Interpreter
Keep Taipy outputs in a separate, read-only folder
Manually review any Taipy-generated text before pasting
Use a provenance tag or prefix for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing wrappers between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and handles model-provider API keys; Taipy has no declared data surfaces, so the pair can leak local files into Open Interpreter’s prompts or downstream model calls. Taipy’s lack of documented storage boundaries makes the shared-workspace path plausible, but not directly evidenced. The blast radius includes sensitive local data and secrets.
conditions: IF Taipy reads or writes files in the same workspace Open Interpreter can access
IF Open Interpreter forwards file contents to a configured model provider
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a dedicated project directory
Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Use separate OS accounts for the two agents
Audit model-provider logging settings
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, with shared state via filesystem across instances. Taipy is a data-engineering automation tool with no concurrency or locking controls documented here, so concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt files or git state. Because the overlap is on mutable resources and Open Interpreter’s defaults are unsafe, the conflict is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF Taipy writes artifacts while Open Interpreter edits or commits the same files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo
Use git branches per agent
Check for file locks before writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate and act on code or shell commands, while Taipy is a data-engineering automation system that may consume upstream outputs. If Taipy treats Open Interpreter’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect pipelines or actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from their roles; no verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Taipy ingests Open Interpreter output without validation
IF Open Interpreter produces commands, configs, or data that Taipy executes
mitigations: Require human review of Open Interpreter outputs before Taipy uses them
Validate schemas and checksums on exchanged artifacts
Log and diff all generated files before execution
Limit Open Interpreter to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add explicit verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and can handle model-provider API keys, creating a local-data governance concern. Taipy has no declared residency, retention, or certification constraints in the profile, so no specific mismatch is evidenced. Because only one agent has documented sensitive-data reach, this is a low compliance risk rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the local filesystem Open Interpreter can access
IF Taipy is later configured to process that regulated data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Document retention and deletion expectations
Use separate storage locations per data class
Review provider-side logging for secrets
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
